answer: A pearl exchange grants one subsidized sale per mature lease. The registrar marks each occupied bed umber and refuses to lease an umber bed twice. To accept a sale it checks the current lease key against a 30-day horizon of uninterrupted occupancy. Changing the key resets the clock. An honest entrant uses 30 bed-days. Registering 1,000 new aliases requires 30,000 bed-days because no lease backs two keys. Buying old keys can evade the reset, so the rule depends on custody as well as honest lease records. Even a real entrant waits 30 days.
